introduction.title: Pocket DS, a small design system
introduction.intro: Install pocket-ds, the peers it needs, and the Inter font. Import the foundation stylesheet before the components.
introduction.installCommand: Install the library and its npm dependencies.
introduction.installNote: Use Node 24. If the app already has React and React DOM, do not install them again: add pocket-ds, sass, and @fontsource/inter only. The package expects React 19. On React 18, append --legacy-peer-deps to the npm command. Sass has to be installed because the styles are published as Sass, not as built CSS.
introduction.fontImports: Import the fonts next to your other global styles, for example in src/main.tsx.
introduction.packageImports: Import the library and start using its components.
introduction.stylesTypes: The pocket-ds/styles import includes its types. If TypeScript says that side-effect import has no type declarations, add declare module "pocket-ds/styles"; to a .d.ts file in the app.
introduction.toolsIntro: What pocket-ds runs on, apart from the components themselves.

tools.name: React and React DOM
tools.detail: The components are plain React. There is no component library underneath.

tools.name: Sass
tools.detail: Compiles the tokens, the foundation stylesheet, and the CSS modules.

tools.name: classnames
tools.detail: Builds the class lists inside the components.

tools.name: Vite
tools.detail: Serves the app in development and builds Storybook.

tools.name: Storybook
tools.detail: Renders these docs, with the docs and accessibility addons.

tools.name: axe-core
tools.detail: Runs the accessibility checks on each story.

tools.name: pnpm
tools.detail: Installs the dependencies. The project uses Node 24.

tools.name: Husky
tools.detail: Git hook that runs Biome, TypeScript, and Vitest before a commit.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.detail: Runs lint, types, tests, the Storybook build, the audit, and the license check.

introduction.dependencies: React, React DOM, and Sass are required. Inter is the typeface used by the tokens. The package does not ship the font files, so load weights 400 and 700 yourself. @fontsource/inter is one way to do that.
introduction.published: This is the version on npm.
introduction.deployed: This is the version of the docs you are reading.

items: Colour, typography, spacing, and breakpoint foundations, with semantic tokens on top of the Sass primitives.
Storybook docs, with locales and viewports that follow the breakpoints.
Unit tests for Badge, Tabs, and Text.
Continuous integration for lint, formatting, types, tests, the Storybook build, the dependency audit, and licenses.
A public package entry for the components and the foundation stylesheet.
This guide, and Vercel hosting with a content security policy.
